title: authored help reaches no estate -- help_file reads only the project's own help/, which devbin never ships
body:
0112 closed at 3a4cd53 as filed: every verb devbin offers now has an authored page in devbin's own tree. None of those pages reaches an estate, and 0.1.7 ships that as its first known limitation. This issue is that limitation, put into work by hv on 2026-09-22.

THE MECHANISM, read at 367309a, whose `lib/` and `bin/` are 0.1.7's byte for byte. `help_file` in `lib/help` looks for a topic's page in one place, the project's own `$DEVBIN_DIR/help/`. What an estate receives is `vendored_paths` in `lib/install`: `bin/devbin` plus every file under `lib/`, and nothing else. `help/` is outside that set by design D5, which the header of `lib/install` states: `config.yaml`, `cmd/` and `help/` are the project's own, and no install or upgrade ever writes them. So in an estate that has not written its own page, every built-in answers `help <cmd>` with the generated stub, and the stub's last line tells the estate to write devbin's page itself: `No authored detail yet. Write it at bin/.devbin/help/<cmd>.md`.

MEASURED IN ESTATES by cc on 2026-09-22, before 0.1.7: `bin/devbin help upgrade` printed the stub in Utilz, Laksa, Conflab and Intent, although devbin carries an 8.5 KB `upgrade.md`, and Utilz, which has release enabled, got the stub for `help release`. 0.1.7 changes neither function, so an estate on 0.1.7 should read the same. That re-measure, in a consumer estate, is the red half of any fix. Devbin's own checkout cannot show this defect, because there `$DEVBIN_DIR/help/` is where devbin's pages live.

IT IS A DESIGN DECISION, NOT A MOVE, which is vc's point in the 0.1.7 note: the pages say things that are only true of devbin. Shipping them means deciding what a shared page says and how a project extends or overrides it.

A proposal to start from, cc's and not ruled: devbin's pages for its built-ins move under `lib/`, so `vendored_paths` ships them with no second list; `help_file` reads the project's page first and devbin's second, so D5 holds and a project's own page still wins; the stub stops telling estates to write devbin's docs; `fleet.md` stays where it is, fleet being devbin's own command; and each moved page is rewritten for a consumer, re-read for truth in a consumer estate, and checked formatter-stable.

FOR dc, THE ADOPTION OWNER. Conflab's own `help/release.md` documents Conflab's own `cmd/release`. It has to retire when Conflab adopts the release core, or, once the project's page is read first, it will answer `help release` in place of the core's page.


RED HALF, MEASURED AT 0.1.7 by cc, 2026-09-23 07:29:49Z to 07:32:44Z. All 16 estates, each running a runtime byte-identical to 0.1.7's (`diff -r` of `bin/.devbin/lib` against `lib/` at 142763d, `cmp` of `bin/devbin`). `bin/devbin help <topic>` for each of devbin's 16 pages plus `test bats`: 272 probes = 16 estates x 17 topics. 203 printed the stub, 26 the project's own page, 39 were not available here, and 4 were a project's own `test.md` answering `help test bats` by the nearest-enclosing-topic rule (Baize, Conflab, Laksa, Lamplight). Utilz, the one estate with release enabled and no page of its own, prints the stub for `help release`. CONTROLS: the 0.1.7 checkout answers all 17 from its own pages, and Conflab's own `help/release.md` answers there. NOTHING WRITTEN: porcelain status was identical before and after in every estate (read with `--no-optional-locks`), and no file was newer than the census start outside pruned deps and build dirs and `.git/objects`.

THE SEVENTEENTH ESTATE, measured the same way later on 2026-09-23. Gtools-geodica, at `~/Devel/cfg`, lies outside the census frame (0116) and is on 0.1.7 too: its runtime is byte-identical to 0.1.7's, it answers 13 of its 17 topics with the stub and 4 are not available, and nothing was written. All 17 estates therefore show the defect: 289 probes, 216 of them the stub.

MEASURED ALONGSIDE, BECAUSE THEY DECIDE THE DESIGN. Each point comes from `help --why` in all 16 estates, the same morning.

1. A SHIPPED PAGE MUST NOT ANSWER WHERE THE PROJECT OWNS THE COMMAND. Intent shadows devbin's `vendor` with its own handler and has no page, so devbin's `vendor.md` would describe a command that does not run there. Gtools and Intent shadow `build` the same way, and arca_cli declares `commands.build.run`.
2. A SHIPPED PAGE ON ITS OWN WOULD HIDE WHAT THE PROJECT ADDED. In Intent, Utilz and Gtools, `check` and `test` resolve through devbin and carry project-declared options (Gtools has six on `check` alone). `check format` and `fmt rust` are overridden by config in Intent and Utilz. None of the three has its own page for these commands. Today's stub lists those options; a bare devbin page would not.
3. 13 OF DEVBIN'S 28 BUILT-INS HAVE NO PAGE ANYWHERE, and 8 of them resolve to devbin in some estate: clean in 10 estates, dormancy 5, fullcycle 4, iex 4, cli 3, repl 3, db 2, server 2. 0112's arm derived its set from devbin's own listing, and that listing belongs to a shell project where those 13 are inactive.

DESIGN, by cc on 2026-09-23. hv delegated 0113 to cc under vc's review. **REVIEWED by vc on 2026-09-23 and approved with changes.** All six changes are taken below: the three required (R1-R3) and the three recommended (R4-R6). vc's two notes are recorded at point 2 and arm 7(d).

1. WHERE. Devbin's pages for its built-ins live at `lib/pages/<cmd>.md`, with sub-topics at `lib/pages/<cmd>.d/<sub>.md`. That is the project tree's shape, so one walk serves both roots. Not `lib/help/`, because `lib/help` is the module. `vendored_paths` ships them with no second list, and in devbin's checkout D12 reads them in place.

2. LOOKUP. `help_file` walks the project's `help/` first, with the existing `.d` descent, and if that walk ends on a file, that file answers. Otherwise the same walk runs over `lib/pages/`, but only when the project does not own the command. "Owns" is ONE predicate, `project_owns_command` in lib/resolve beside `has_project_handler`: a project handler (a file, or a mapped `handler:`) or a command-level `run:`. Doctor's shadow report already makes this same check inline (`_shadow_hits`), and it moves to calling the predicate (R4). The walk is one function taking a root. A project page always wins (D5). A command the project owns but has no page for gets the generated answer, which names its true origin.
   - Consequence of project-first: a project's own `test.md` hides a more specific shipped sub-page. That is the chosen rule, it is armed at 7(d), and it is moot until a shipped page has sub-pages (vc's note 2).

3. THE TRAILER. A shipped page is followed by `In this project:`, then two blocks:
   - The command's `--why` block (`_print_command <cmd> yes`).
   - The command's options that are NOT offered here, each with its reason. This is the walk `_print_unavailable` already makes, scoped to the one command rather than copied.
   The second block is R1's point. `command_options` lists ACTIVE options only, so without it a disabled option would vanish from the trailer while the page above still describes it. A project's own page is still printed whole and alone.

4. THE STUB. For a devbin built-in with no shipped page, the stub says devbin ships no page for it yet and points at `help --why`. It never tells an estate to write devbin's page. `Write it at bin/.devbin/help/<cmd>.md` stays for commands the project owns or declared.

5. WHAT SHIPS. Fifteen pages ship, one for each built-in that has a page:
   - Moved to `lib/pages/` and rewritten for a consumer: build, devbin, docs, doctor, fmt, infra, install, new, release, shell-init, upgrade, vendor and version.
   - NEW consumer pages: check and test.
   Devbin's own pages stay in `bin/.devbin/help/`:
   - fleet: devbin's own command.
   - test and `test.d/bats`: devbin's own handler and option.
   - check: devbin's own declared gates.
   In devbin's tree these answer first, as any project's own pages do.

6. WHAT A SHIPPED PAGE SAYS. A shipped page says only what is true wherever devbin's implementation of that command runs, since that is the only place it answers:
   - no path into devbin's source (`docs/`, `intent/`, `tests/`, a checkout's `lib/`);
   - no devbin-own config (bats, shell-gate);
   - every issue or design citation qualified, as `devbin#NNNN` or "devbin design Dn";
   - the invocation spelled `bin/devbin`.
   Arm 7(h) holds this, so it does not rest on this sentence (R6). Before it ships, each page is also re-read for truth in a consumer estate.
   FORMAT (R3): every shipped page must be prettier-stable AND print as authored, so prettier's fixed point is the same bytes `cat` shows. Every terminal-aligned block (the step table, option lists, exit codes) is therefore indented four spaces after a blank line. Markdown reads that as a code block, and prettier leaves code blocks alone. Inside a list item four spaces is continuation text, which prettier reflows, so there the untagged fence is the rule rather than the fallback (vc, 2026-09-23). Everywhere else an untagged fence is the fallback. A fence never carries a language tag, which would invite prettier to format the inside. The current pages are NOT to be passed through `prettier --write`, which collapses their alignment. Measured 2026-09-23 with prettier 3.9.8, default config: 16 of devbin's 17 pages fail `prettier --check` today, and shell-init.md passes because its aligned lines are indented four spaces. Intent declares markdown to the canon staged-format guard, which checks every staged `.md`, so pages moved as they are would get the next sweep refused at Intent.

7. ARMS. Each runs red first against 0.1.7, in INSTALLED fixtures. `mkproj` installs through the real installer, so a fixture holds exactly what `vendored_paths` ships.
   - (a) and (f), together (R2). The fixtures activate ALL 28 built-ins: elixir and rust declared, and the six opt-ins enabled, using two fixtures if one cannot hold them all. (a): every built-in with a page in `lib/pages/` answers with it plus the trailer. (f): every other built-in answers with the honest stub, never "Write it at". Together they assert they exercised `builtin_commands`' full count: the pages and the stubs sum to the catalogue's 28. A floor alone would let one fall out again, which is how 0112's population narrowed. (a) is the arm that would have caught 0113 at 0112's close: documentation.bats's derived arm runs only in DEVBIN_HOME, where 0113 cannot show.
   - (b) A project page wins, printed whole with no trailer.
   - (c) All three facts of `project_owns_command` are driven, each getting the generated answer and never devbin's page (R5): a handler file (Intent's `vendor` shape), a mapped `handler:`, and a command-level `run:` (arca_cli's `build`).
   - (d) The two-root case: a project's own `test.md` answers `help test <sub>`. The shipped sub-page it hides is PLANTED in the fixture's vendored `lib/pages/test.d/`, since devbin ships none, and the arm says so (vc's note 1).
   - (e) The trailer names a project-declared option and an overridden one, each with its origin, and names a DISABLED option with its reason, not merely by leaving it out (R1).
   - (g) `prettier --check` over `lib/pages/` under the default config (R3). It asserts its denominator, the count of files prettier checked equal to the pages shipped, so a future `.prettierignore` line cannot let it pass having checked nothing (vc, 2026-09-23). It runs wherever prettier is installed and prints its skip where it is not. That covers the place it matters: the release cut's `test all` gate runs on the machine the sweep runs from. Whether CI's Ubuntu leg also installs prettier is hv's call on cost.
   - (h) A source arm over `lib/pages/` for point 6 (R6): no `docs/`, `intent/` or `tests/` path, no devbin-own config, and no unqualified issue citation. Its positive control plants each one and sees it refused.

8. SEAM PROSE. These describe where help comes from and change with it: lib/install's header (D5), config.reference.yaml's help section, docs/authoring-commands.md, README's seam lines, ARCHITECTURE-shell.md, and new.md where it describes `help/`. vc did not check this list for completeness, so the build greps for every other description of where help lives.

9. OUT OF SCOPE: pages for the 13 built-ins that have none. They are issue 0115, filed as a finding against 0112's close (vc agreed, 2026-09-23); when it is built is hv's call. Until then, 7(f) keeps their stubs honest.

10. FOR dc, UNCHANGED. Conflab's own `help/release.md` must retire when Conflab adopts the release core. Otherwise, with the project read first, it will answer `help release` in place of the core's page.

## Resolution

Fixed at 719e8a1, together with 0118. Ships in 0.1.8.

- WHAT CHANGED. Devbin's pages ship at lib/pages/: thirteen moved from devbin's own bin/.devbin/help/ and rewritten for a consumer's tree, and two new ones, check and test. help reads the project's help/ first, then devbin's pages, and devbin's page answers only where the project does not own the command. Owning is one predicate, project_owns_command in lib/resolve, which doctor's shadow report now calls as well. A devbin page is followed by "In this project:", the command as it resolves there. A built-in with no page gets an honest stub, not an instruction to write devbin's page.
- RED FIRST, AND WHERE IT COULD NOT BE. At 0.1.7 the catalogue, trailer, prettier and source arms failed for the reasons they name. The others pass there trivially, since no page ships, so each was driven red by a mutant of the build instead: 23 of cc's, 20 killed, and the 3 survivors closed by the two arms written for them. vc's ten mutants agree.
- THE TEST-CHECK CRITIC found a false green before landing. The trailer arm asserted the word "disabled", which check.md's own prose says, so the trailer's reason could vanish with every arm green; the header, which check.md and test.md quote, likewise. An assertion on a word a shipped page can say is satisfied by the page, not by the code under test. The trailer is now matched as whole lines, and five weaker places were fixed in the same change. Rerun against the fixed arms, 21 of the critic's 22 mutants are killed, each by the arm aimed at it; the 22nd, prettier off PATH with CI set, skips naming hv's ruling, as designed, and fails once the call names no ruling. Seven more of cc's, aimed at the new assertions and at the arms' own checkers, are killed too. vc's FINAL checks passed on the final patch, its M8, M9 and H13 and the critic's critical each killed by the arms.
- REVIEW. vc reviewed the design (R1 to R6), the build, and the final patch.
- THE SUITE. The full suite on the final content, byte-identical to what landed: 1..1623, 1623 ok, 0 not ok, 4 skipped (the two machine-bound tty branches and harness's two skip-branch arms), indices in order, rc=0. The six affected files alone: 1..224, 224 ok.
- LEFT OPEN. The 13 built-ins with no page are 0115. Two defects the build's code review found outside 0113's lines are filed separately: 0127 (the vendored set's find errors) and 0128 (D2's project tiers).
